page: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is an entry-to-mid-tier instance within the High Performance family, utilizing AMD EPYC x86_64 processors. It provides 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with support for AVX, AES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets. System memory is configured at 8.0 GB of RAM, offering 2.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no dedicated GPUs and comes provisioned with 180 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark outcomes show moderate CPU baseline compute alongside restrained memory throughput. Multi-core and single-core stress-ng tests perform in the average middle tier at 9232.12 and 2306.16 points, respectively, with cryptographic operations demonstrating steady capability on PassMark encryption tests (3693.88). However, the shared-vCPU configuration and memory subsystem show bottlenecks under high demand: uncached read bandwidth drops to 17.9 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth to 12.56 GB/sec, placing memory bandwidth in the lower decile. Geekbench single-core (1119.0) and multi-core (3378.0) scores, along with Redis SET operations (3.94 million ops/sec) and static web serving (2.66 GB/sec), reflect typical shared-resource constraints.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance targets density over peak computational intensity. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with bundled local NVMe storage provides solid general utility for small-to-medium tasks without incurring the costs associated with dedicated-core or massive memory profiles. Workloads best matched to this profile include lightweight web applications, staging environments, modest internal utilities, asynchronous background task workers, and developmental build tasks that do not require high sustained memory bandwidth.
description: Vultr vhp-4c-8gb-amd is a High Performance series instance powered by AMD EPYC x86_64 processors running at 2.0 GHz. The virtual server is configured with 4 shared vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of system memory, and 180 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage, without GPU accelerators. Benchmark evaluations place raw compute in the average middle range via stress-ng, while memory bandwidth tests and Geekbench scores reflect lower-tier performance typical of shared virtualization environments. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers balanced resource distribution for non-memory-intensive workloads. Given its balanced resource footprint and bundled fast storage, the instance serves effectively for lightweight web serving, staging environments, microservices, internal automation tooling, and general-purpose development pipelines.
